Messages.Author: Ian Lee
Messages.Body:
>But there's no reason for them to print on the card:
>"Haste. (Creature can tap or attack the turn it comes out)."

There is a reason. The shortcut terms, don't remember what the proper word for
them is, help solidify the rules. One term will always mean the same thing in
every situation. When you refer to that term, you always mean the same thing
everyone else does because it has become part of the rules rather than
individual card text. Because it always means precisely the same thing, you
don't get into situations where two cards are almost exactly written the same
way but aren't, which leads them to being played differently in obscure
situations.

When they first started doing it, I thought it was annoying and redundant too.
But, I read an article where someone talked about these shortcut terms. I
don't recall much from it, but I believe it convinced me not to be bothered by
the explanatory text. I don't play much, so you would think I'd be less used
to it and notice it more than players who see it every day. But, I hardly
notice it.

I think the answer, given what Ian is saying is, "No, they can't." You're missing
the point. It's a matter of personal perception, of course, but WotC apparently
*did* believe it really caused a problem in the past - to beginners trying to learn
the game who would find all of these new terms they're unfamiliar with difficult to
memorize. Getting people into a complex strategy game (and yes, in the context of the
general population, Magic is a complex strategy game) is a matter of making it as easy
for them as possible. You may see it as "dumbing down" but WotC sees it as more
new customers and a few slightly-irritated-but-still-buying-the-game older customers.
Add it up any way you please, it means more bucks to them.

Ian is just stating why, given the fact that they're going to insist on printing the
specifics of the rules on every card, they bothered to give those reused templates names
at all.

> Heck, I haven't seen a new card with Banding (I have friends who still play,
> every now and then I take a look at their cards), but if they put the italic text
> after that, they'd need to print awfully small, or have a fold-out page :)

I believe they discarded Banding as card mechanic, based on something like too much
complexity for its entertainment value. If so, I agree. It really wasn't worth using.

Messages.Author: Ian Lee
Messages.Body:
>Ian is just stating why, given the fact that they're going to insist on
>printing the
>specifics of the rules on every card, they bothered to give those reused
>templates names
>at all.

I think I'll try another go at why they use both the game term and the
explanatory text.

The shortcut term isn't on the individual cards to make those cards easier to
understand or play. The shortcut terms are to make the game easier to
understand and play on a more general level ... while the explanatory text
describes more fully what the individual card does.

Constantly repeated concepts/phrases can be summed up in gamespeak with one
word on a rules level, design level, conversational level. That we speak of
"haste" instead of "can attack and use tap effects the turn it comes into play"
is useful whatever the cards say, for example.
